records.inclusion_criteria: 1. Aged 18 to 65 years (inclusive), male or female; 2. Diagnosis: Confirmed diagnosis of autoimmune generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) that meets the clinical classification criteria for Class II, III, or IVa as defined by the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America (MGFA). Patients must have a documented history of seropositivity for anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle-specific kinase (MuSK) antibodies, or test positive for these antibodies during the screening period; 3. Disease Severity: Total MG-ADL score >6, with more than 50% of the total score derived from non-ocular items; 4. Concomitant Medications: Patients receiving acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChEIs) and/or oral corticosteroids (OCS) or immunosuppressive therapies (ISTs) at screening are permitted, subject to the following criteria: (1) Stable dose of AChEIs for at least 2 weeks; (2) Stable dose of OCS <=20 mg/day for at least 1 month; (3) Azathioprine (AZA), mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), tacrolimus, or methotrexate must have been initiated at least 6 months prior to ICF signing and maintained at a stable dose for at least 3 months; 5. Neurological status stable for >=30 days prior to the baseline assessment; 6. Adequate hepatic and renal function: Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) <=2.0×ULN; Serum total bilirubin <=1.2×ULN, or <=3.0×ULN in patients with a confirmed diagnosis of Gilbert's syndrome (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia); Serum creatinine (SCr) <=1.5×ULN, or estimated creatinine clearance (CrCL) >=60 mL/min calculated according to the Cockcroft-Gault formula: CrCL (mL/min) = [(140 − age) × weight (kg)] / [72 × SCr (mg/dL)] (× 0.85 if female); SCr (mg/dL) = SCr (µmol/L) / 88.4; 7. Contraception and Pregnancy Requirements: All male subjects and female subjects of childbearing potential must use a medically acceptable method of contraception throughout the treatment period and for 1 week after the last dose of study treatment. Female subjects of childbearing potential who are premenopausal (e.g., who have not been amenorrheic for at least 1 year, or who have not undergone surgical sterilization) must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days prior to the initiation of treatment. (If the serum pregnancy test obtained during the screening period is >7 days prior to the first dose, a serum pregnancy test must be performed prior to the first dose; subjects may only be enrolled upon obtaining a negative result). Female subjects must not be lactating. Male subjects are prohibited from donating sperm during the study period and for 1 week after the last dose of study treatment; 8. Voluntary written informed consent has been obtained, and the subject agrees to comply with the study protocol and visit schedule.
records.exclusion_criteria: 1. Presence of neurological diseases or systemic autoimmune diseases other than gMG; 2. History of thymectomy within 12 months prior to screening, planned thymectomy during the study period, or gMG caused by thymoma; 3. History of malignancy within 2 years prior to screening, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin, carcinoma in situ of the cervix, ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast, localized squamous cell carcinoma, and any other malignancy confirmed by the investigator as having achieved a cure through surgery or other treatments; 4. History of severe infection or potential risk of severe infection, specifically including: (1) Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, syphilis, or Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection (subjects with a history of past infection who are deemed cured by the investigator or specialist are eligible). HBsAg or HBcAb positive with HBV-DNA levels above the upper limit of normal (ULN) at the local laboratory (i.e., subjects who are HBsAg or HBcAb positive but HBV-DNA negative are eligible, provided they receive anti-hepatitis B therapy during the study). HCV antibody positive with HCV-RNA levels above the ULN at the local laboratory or qualitatively positive (i.e., subjects who are HCV-RNA negative are eligible); (2) History of organ, allogeneic stem cell, or bone marrow transplantation and/or anti-rejection therapy; (3) Systemic chronic, recurrent, or severe infection (e.g., infectious pneumonia, sepsis) within 90 days prior to screening; (4) uncontrolled systemic active bacterial, fungal, or viral infection within 4 weeks prior to screening; 5. Subjects who have received a live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks prior to screening, or who plan to receive a live attenuated vaccine during the study period or within 4 weeks after the end of study treatment; 6. Subjects who have previously received Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor therapy, for either malignant or autoimmune disease indications; 7. Any other medical condition or complication that, in the investigator's judgment, may adversely affect the subject's participation in the study, including but not limited to: (1) Short life expectancy due to pre-existing medical conditions, as determined by the investigator; (2) Any other medical condition or complication that prevents the evaluation of the primary efficacy endpoint or may adversely affect the subject's participation in the study, as determined by the investigator; (3) Any severe and/or uncontrolled systemic disease that, in the investigator's judgment, makes the subject unsuitable for participation in this study (including uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes mellitus of >=Grade 2 CTCAE, unstable angina, congestive heart failure, respiratory disease requiring continuous oxygen therapy, severe vascular thrombosis, uncontrolled severe hemorrhage or bleeding from vital organs or known platelet dysfunction, severe hepatic, renal, or metabolic diseases such as liver cirrhosis or renal failure); (4) Impaired cardiac function, including meeting the criteria for New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class >=2, or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50% as shown by echocardiography; or clinically significant abnormalities on the screening electrocardiogram (ECG), mainly including atrial fibrillation/flutter, Mobitz type II second-degree atrioventricular (AV) block, third-degree AV block, CTCAE >=Grade 2 bradycardia, and QTcF (QTc corrected by Fridericia's formula) >=480 ms on >=3 independent ECGs. (Note: NYHA functional class 2 is defined as slight limitation of physical activity; ordinary physical activity results in undue fatigue, palpitation, dyspnea, or anginal pain, while the subject is comfortable at rest. The QTcF is calculated as QT/[RR^0.33], where RR = 60/heart rate); 8. History of cerebral infarction or intracranial hemorrhage (subjects with lacunar infarction who, in the investigator's judgment, do not preclude enrollment in this study, are excluded); 9. History of myocardial infarction within 180 days; 10. Subjects who have received any investigational drug within 3 months prior to screening or within 5 half-lives of any other investigational drug, whichever is longer; 11. Subjects who have received any of the following treatments within the specified timeframe prior to the baseline assessment: (1) FcRn antagonists (e.g., efgartigimod) within 3 months prior to screening; (2) Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies (e.g., ofatumumab, ocrelizumab, or rituximab) within 6 months prior to screening, or peripheral blood B-lymphocyte counts have not recovered to normal levels after treatment; (3) Prior treatment with total lymphoid irradiation, mitoxantrone (associated with cardiotoxicity or a cumulative dose of >=120 mg/m^2), or other potent immunosuppressive therapies with a prolonged duration of effect; 12. Subjects who have undergone major surgery (typically defined as Grade III or above according to institutional regulations) or experienced severe trauma within 4 weeks prior to screening; 13. Subjects who require treatment during the study with the following medications: strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers (see Appendix 4), or sensitive substrates of OATP1B3 (see Appendix 4); 14. Subjects who have received anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents within 7 days prior to screening or within 5 half-lives of the study drug, whichever is longer; 15. Conditions that may affect the subject's ability to swallow study medication, or conditions that may significantly affect the absorption or pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of the study drug, including but not limited to uncontrolled nausea and vomiting, and short bowel syndrome; 16. Presence of disease symptoms that may interfere with the administration of the investigational medicinal product (IMP), or unresolved toxicities from prior therapy that may confound the assessment of adverse events; or underlying conditions, alcohol abuse, or drug abuse/dependence that may compromise compliance with study procedures; 17. Known hypersensitivity to rocbrutinib or any of its excipients (including microcrystalline cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate, fumaric acid, and gastric-soluble film-coating premix); 18. The investigator considers that there are any other circumstances that would make the subject unsuitable for participation in this study.

Inclusion Criteria for Patients with MS: 1. Diagnosis of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS) according to the 2017 revised McDonald criteria, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS), and active secondary progressive MS. 2. Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score <= 6.0. 3. At least one documented relapse within 1 year prior to screening, or at least two documented relapses within 2 years prior to screening, or active gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the brain within 1 year prior to screening. 4. Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) score >= 6, with ocular domain score less than 50% of the total score. 5. Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) score >= 8, with at least 4 items scoring at least 2 points each. 6. As judged by the investigator, has a suboptimal response to current stable MG therapy. Stable therapy is defined as: a) If taking acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, the subject must have been on a stable dose and regimen for at least 2 weeks prior to screening; b) If using glucocorticoids, the subject must have been on a stable dose and regimen for at least 4 weeks prior to screening; c) If the subject is receiving immunosuppressive therapy, the subject must have been on immunosuppressive therapy for >= 6 months and on a stable dose for >= 3 months prior to screening. Permitted immunosuppressants are azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, methotrexate, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, cyclophosphamide, etc. Or, has discontinued corticosteroids and/or immunosuppressants due to intolerance or lack of efficacy at least 4 weeks prior to screening. Experienced at least 2 clinically documented relapses within 2 years prior to screening, or at least 1 clinically documented relapse within 1 year prior to screening. 4. Relapse occurred >= 2 times after discontinuing medication upon meeting discontinuation criteria. 4. Serum TRAb (TSH receptor antibody) level >= 3 times the upper limit of the normal range (>= 5 IU/L). 5. Positive CD19 expression on peripheral blood B cells (as detected by flow cytometry). 6. Willing to participate in this clinical study, sign the informed consent form, and adhere well to the treatment and follow-up plan. (Discontinuation criteria are defined as: continuous anti-thyroid drug therapy for >= 18 months, and maintaining normal thyroid function for >= 6 months, with both TRAb and TSI (thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin) negative. Relapse is defined as the recurrence of hyperthyroidism along with positive TRAb/TSI after discontinuing medication upon meeting discontinuation criteria.) Inclusion Criteria for Autoimmune Encephalitis (AE): 1. Meets the diagnostic criteria for autoimmune encephalitis (e.g., positive anti-NMDA receptor antibodies, typical clinical manifestations, and imaging/cerebrospinal fluid support). 2. Persistent neurological deficits (e.g., psychiatric/behavioral abnormalities, seizures, autonomic dysfunction) or neurological function score (e.g., modified Rankin Score >= 3 points). Inclusion Criteria for Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (AIHA): 1. Confirmed diagnosis of AIHA: Meets the typical diagnostic criteria for AIHA (decreased hemoglobin, elevated reticulocytes, positive Coombs test, etc.). Refractory/Relapsed disease: Failure of conventional therapy, defined as ineffective or intolerant to at least two standard therapies (e.g., glucocorticoids + rituximab, immunosuppressants). Persistent severe hemolysis: Hemoglobin < 8 g/dL, dependent on blood transfusions for maintenance, or recurrent life-threatening hemolytic crises. Inclusion Criteria for Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP): 1. Confirmed diagnosis of ITP: Meets internationally accepted diagnostic criteria (persistent platelet count < 100 × 10⁹/L, excluding other causes of thrombocytopenia such as drugs, infection, malignancy). Refractory/Relapsed disease: Failure of standard therapy, defined as ineffective or dependent on high-dose maintenance with at least two first-line treatments (e.g., glucocorticoids + intravenous immunoglobulin/TPO receptor agonists). Ineffective or relapsed after rituximab therapy (applicable for adult patients). Recurrence after splenectomy (applicable for splenectomy candidates). 3. High-risk bleeding tendency: Persistent platelet count < 30 × 10⁹/L accompanied by active bleeding (e.g., mucosal bleeding, hematuria) or high bleeding risk (e.g., advanced age, hypertension).

History of allogeneic bone marrow or stem cell transplantation or solid organ transplantation (e.g., kidney, lung, heart transplant) or planned future such transplantation. 11. Prior history of autologous or allogeneic CAR T-cell therapy. 12. History or current presence of significant cardiovascular dysfunction, including: a) Signs or symptoms of congestive heart failure corresponding to New York Heart Association (NYHA) class >= III within 12 months prior to screening; b) Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50% as shown by echocardiography (assessed at screening); c) Myocardial infarction, unstable angina, uncontrolled or symptomatic atrial arrhythmias, any ventricular arrhythmia, or other clinically significant heart disease within 6 months prior to screening; d) Pulmonary hypertension, including secondary pulmonary hypertension, with WHO functional class > 2. 13. Severe asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Mild or moderate asthma or COPD on stable treatment may be considered after discussion with the Medical Monitor. 14. Presence of uncontrolled infection at screening. records.inclusion_criteria: 1.Age >=18 years <=80 years,No gender restriction; 2.MGFA classification type IIa-IVb; 3.Voluntary participation in the study: understanding and awareness of the study and voluntary signing of the informed consent form; 4.Meeting the diagnosis of myasthenia gravis; 5.Patients with moderate to severe, refractory MG who are assessed by researchers as having poor disease control after conventional immunotherapy and biologic targeted therapy: meeting at least one of the following three criteria: (1)Having received adequate doses and full courses of at least two conventional immunotherapy drugs (including corticosteroids and non-steroidal immunosuppressants), and having undergone treatment with at least one biological targeted drug, with no change or worsening in post-intervention status (PIS); (2)After receiving adequate doses and full courses of treatment with at least two conventional immunotherapy drugs, and having undergone treatment with at least one biological targeted drug, the Post-Intervention Status (PIS) shows improvement, but the MG-ADL score remains >=6 points for at least six months; (3)After receiving adequate doses and full courses of treatment with at least two conventional immunotherapy drugs, and having undergone treatment with at least one biological targeted drug, the Post-Intervention Status (PIS) shows remission or improvement, but there are still >=2 exacerbations of disease symptoms (MG-ADL score >=6) per year; 6.MG-ADL score >=6 or QMG score >=11 at screening and baseline, with ocular muscle score less than 50% of the total score; 7.Male study participants must agree to use contraception during the treatment period and for 2 years after the last dose of the study treatment, and must also agree not to donate sperm throughout the entire study period; 8.If the participant is a woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP), she must agree to use contraception during the treatment period and for 2 years after the last dose of the study treatment. At screening, the participant’s serum pregnancy test result must be negative; before the first dose of the study drug at baseline, the urine pregnancy test result must be confirmed negative.
records.exclusion_criteria: 1.Any medical or psychiatric condition that the investigator deems may endanger the study participant or affect their ability to participate in the study; or any condition the investigator considers associated with poor compliance; 2.Females who are breastfeeding or pregnant, or plan to become pregnant at any time during the 2 years period after receiving CAR-T therapy, or have a history of spontaneous or induced abortion within 4 weeks prior to screening; 3.Study participants with clinically relevant active infections (e.g., sepsis, pneumonia, or abscess) or severe infections (requiring hospitalization or antibiotic treatment) within 4 weeks prior to screening; 4.Thymectomy within 6 months prior to baseline or planned thymectomy during the study period, or thymoma requiring chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy at any time; 5.Study participants who received live attenuated vaccines within 8 weeks prior to screening; or plan to receive live vaccines within 8 weeks after treatment; 6.Study participants who received prior rituximab treatment within 6 months before screening; 7.Treatment with tocilizumab, eculizumab within 3 months prior to screening; 8.Intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, or immunotherapy within 4 weeks prior to screening; 9.Known severe underlying diseases, such as liver or kidney dysfunction, hematologic disorders, prior severe cardiovascular diseases, severe hypertension, diabetes, or poorly controlled blood pressure or blood glucose; 10.Unresected thymoma; 11.Participants with a positive immunological test for Mycobacterium tuberculosis can be enrolled if they meet the following conditions simultaneously:(1)No radiological evidence of active tuberculosis.(2)No signs of tuberculosis intoxication (such as low-grade fever, fatigue, night sweats, decreased appetite, weight loss, etc.), or respiratory symptoms (such as cough, sputum production for more than 2 weeks, or with hemoptysis, blood-streaked sputum); 12.Participants who are positive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) or hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb) and have a quantitative level of hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA in peripheral blood above the lower limit of detection; participants who are positive for hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody and have a quantitative level of HCV RNA above the lower limit of detection; participants who are positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody; participants who are positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA; participants who are positive for both specific and non-specific antibodies to Treponema pallidum (the causative agent of syphilis); 13.Other circumstances in which the investigator considers the participant to be ineligible for enrollment in this study.

records.inclusion_criteria: General Inclusion Criteria for All Patients: 1. The subject voluntarily agrees to participate in this trial and signs the informed consent form. 2. Age >= 18 years and <= 70 years, regardless of gender. 3. Organ function and laboratory tests: a) Liver function: Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) <= 3 × upper limit of normal (ULN), total bilirubin (TBIL) <= 2 × ULN (excluding Gilbert’s syndrome). b) Renal function: Creatinine <= 1.5 × ULN or creatinine clearance >= 40 ml/min. c) Complete blood count: Neutrophil count >= 1 × 10^9/L, hemoglobin >= 60 g/L, platelet count >= 20 × 10^9/L, lymphocyte count > 0.3 × 10^9/L. d) Coagulation function: International normalized ratio (INR) <= 1.5 × ULN, or prothrombin time (PT) <= 1.5 × ULN. e) Oxygen saturation (SpO2) at rest in room air >= 92%. f) Echocardiogram showing left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) >= 50%. Female subjects of childbearing potential must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test at screening. Females of childbearing potential must agree to use effective contraception from at least 28 days prior to the start of lymphodepletion until 12 months after RC-01 infusion. Males of childbearing potential must agree to use effective barrier contraception from the start of lymphodepletion until 12 months after RC-01 infusion and should not donate semen or sperm during the entire trial period. Inclusion Criteria for SLE Patients: 1. A confirmed diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) based on the 2019 European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR)/American College of Rheumatology (ACR) classification criteria or the 2012 Systemic Lupus Erythematosus International Collaborating Clinics (SLICC) criteria. 2. Patients must have received treatment with corticosteroids in combination with immunosuppressants and/or biologics for at least 2 months prior to screening, with a stable dose for more than 2 weeks, and the disease must still be active (i.e., prior treatment with corticosteroids + immunosuppressants or corticosteroids + immunosuppressants + biologics; any single agent use of the above medications does not qualify). Oral corticosteroids must meet the following criteria: 1) Prednisone (or equivalent) ≥ 7.5 mg/day; 2) There is no minimum daily dose requirement for corticosteroids when used in combination with immunosuppressants and/or biologics. 3. Positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) test at screening, and/or positive anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-ds-DNA) antibody, and/or positive anti-Smith antibody. 4. A SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) score > 6 at screening, with a "clinical" SLEDAI-2K score >= 4. Note: The "clinical" SLEDAI-2K score excludes points attributable to any urine or laboratory test results (including immunological markers): Includes clinical items such as: arthritis, myositis, rash, alopecia, mucosal ulcers, pleuritis, pericarditis, or vasculitis; Excludes points attributable to fever, SLE headache, and organic brain syndrome. For patients with lupus nephritis, if there is proteinuria > 0.5 g/24 hours or UPCR > 500 mg/g; or active urinary sediment (excluding infection, defined as > 5 red blood cells/high power field or > 5 white blood cells/high power field, or red blood cell casts, or white blood cell casts), the requirement for a "clinical" SLEDAI-2K score >= 4 may be waived. 5.Physician’s Global Assessment (PGA) score >= 1.0 (0-3 visual analog scale). Inclusion Criteria for SSc Patients: 1. A diagnosis of systemic sclerosis (SSc) based on the 2013 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. 2. A diagnosis of diffuse cutaneous SSc at screening. 3. Evidence of active disease, defined by at least one of the following: a) New onset of SSc within the past 2 years prior to screening. b) New skin involvement or worsening in two new body areas within the past 6 months (as defined by the modified Rodnan skin score [mRSS] assessing 17 body areas). c) New involvement or worsening in the chest or abdomen within the past 6 months. d) Worsening of skin thickening within the past 6 months (mRSS >= 2). e) At least one recorded instance of tendon friction rub within the past 3 months and at screening. f) A comparison of pulmonary function tests at screening with those conducted within the past 12 months, showing an absolute decline in FVC of >= 5% of predicted value or an absolute decline in DLCO of >= 10% of predicted value, along with worsening respiratory symptoms. g) A comparison of high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) at screening with that conducted within the past 12 months, showing progression of interstitial lung disease (ILD). h) At screening, forced vital capacity (FVC) >= 50% and diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) >= 45% of predicted value. i) Ineffectiveness of standard treatment or relapse after disease remission. Standard treatment is defined as the use of corticosteroids (prednisone > 0.5 mg/kg/day or equivalent) and cyclophosphamide, along with any of the following immunomodulatory agents: antimalarials, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, methotrexate, leflunomide, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and/or biologics such as rituximab or belimumab, with a cumulative treatment duration of > 6 months. Inclusion Criteria for AAV Patients: 1. A diagnosis of ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) according to the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria, including microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). 2. Positive ANCA-related antibody testing in the past or at screening (either myeloperoxidase anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody [MPO-ANCA] positive or proteinase 3 anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody [PR3-ANCA] positive). 3. A Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS) indicating at least one major item, or at least three minor items, or at least two renal items. 4. Failure of prior standard of care (SOC) treatment, defined by any of the following: a) Failure to achieve remission after at least 4 months of treatment with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide or rituximab; b) Disease relapse after previously achieving remission; c) Prior treatment with SOC for at least 6 months, including corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, methotrexate, leflunomide, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and biologics (such as rituximab, mepolizumab, or avacopan), but still having active disease. Inclusion Criteria for IIM Patients: 1. A diagnosis of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM) according to the 2017 ACR/EULAR classification criteria (including probable or definite diagnosis with a probability of >= 55%), with subtypes including dermatomyositis (DM), antisynthetase syndrome (ASS), and immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM). 2. Patients must be in an active phase, defined as having at least 2 abnormal findings among the following six core indicators:Muscle strength decline (MMT-8 < 142),Physician Global Assessment (PhGA, 10 cm VAS) >= 2 cm,Patient Global Assessment (PtGA, 10 cm VAS) >= 2 cm,Extramuscular disease activity overall score (using the MDAAT scoring tool for extramuscular disease activity) >= 2 cm,Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ) >= 0.25,Creatine kinase (CK) enzyme levels >= 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN). 3. Positive testing for myositis-specific autoantibodies (including anti-ARS antibodies, anti-Jo-1 antibodies, anti-HA/YRS antibodies, anti-Zo antibodies, anti-EJ antibodies, anti-PL-7 antibodies, anti-OJ antibodies, anti-KS antibodies, anti-PL-12 antibodies, anti-Mi-2 antibodies, anti-TIF1 antibodies, anti-MDA5 antibodies, anti-SAE antibodies, anti-NXP2 antibodies, anti-SRP antibodies, and anti-HMGCR antibodies) in the past or at screening. 4. Ineffectiveness of standard treatment or relapse after disease remission. Standard treatment is defined as the use of corticosteroids (prednisone > 1 mg/kg/day or equivalent) and/or at least one immunomodulatory agent, such as antimalarials, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and/or biologics such as rituximab and belimumab, with a cumulative treatment duration of at least 6 months. Inclusion Criteria for pSS Patients: 1. A diagnosis of primary Sjögren’s syndrome (pSS) according to the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. 2. Positive testing for anti-SSA/Ro antibodies in the past or at screening. 3. A European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) Sjögren’s Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) score of >= 6 at screening. 4. Ineffectiveness of standard treatment or relapse after disease remission. Standard treatment is defined as the use of corticosteroids (prednisone > 1 mg/kg/day or equivalent) and/or at least one immunomodulatory agent, such as antimalarials, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and/or biologics such as rituximab and belimumab, with a cumulative treatment duration of at least 6 months. Inclusion Criteria for MS Patients: 1. A diagnosis of relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS) according to the revised 2017 McDonald criteria, including clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), and active secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS). 2. Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of <= 6.0. 3. At least one relapse recorded in the year prior to screening, or at least two relapses recorded in the two years prior to screening, or the presence of active gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the brain within the year prior to screening. 4. Neurological symptoms must have been stable for at least 30 days prior to screening. Inclusion Criteria for NMOSD Patients: 1. A diagnosis of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) according to the 2015 International NMO Diagnosis Group (IPND) criteria. 2. Positive testing for aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G (AQP4-IgG) during the screening period or a prior medical record indicating AQP4-IgG positivity. 3. At least two clinically documented relapses within the two years prior to screening, or at least one clinically documented relapse within the year prior to screening. 4. At least one immunosuppressive agent has been used for more than one year, but symptoms remain difficult to control. 5. Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of <= 7.5. 6. Patients must have received stable treatment prior to screening (if applicable), defined as follows: a) Immunosuppressants: Patients must have been on a stable dose of immunosuppressive medications (such as azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, methotrexate, etc.) for at least 8 weeks prior to screening; b) Corticosteroids: Patients must have had a stable dose for at least 4 weeks prior to screening; c) If patients have received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) infusion or plasmapheresis treatment, the last treatment must have been completed more than 4 weeks prior to screening. Inclusion Criteria for MG Patients: 1. Patients diagnosed with generalized myasthenia gravis (MG). 2. Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America (MGFA) clinical classification of type II, III, or IV. 3. Positive serological testing for acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-Ab), muscle-specific kinase antibodies (MuSK-Ab), or low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein antibodies (LRP4-Ab) at screening, or a prior medical record indicating positivity for AChR-Ab, MuSK-Ab, or LRP4-Ab. 4. Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) score of >= 6, with the ocular-related score being less than 50% of the total score. 5. Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) score of ≥ 8, with at least 4 items scoring 2 or more. ue to intolerance or lack of efficacy must have done so at least 4 weeks prior to screening.
records.exclusion_criteria: Patients will be excluded from participating in this study if they meet any of the following criteria: 1. A primary diagnosis of an autoimmune disease that is complementary to the disease under study, which, in the investigator's opinion, could confound the efficacy evaluation of the disease under study. 2. For SLE patients: Uncontrolled lupus crisis within 8 weeks prior to screening, including but not limited to rapidly progressive lupus nephritis, severe neuropsychiatric lupus, severe hemolytic anemia, severe immune thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, severe cardiac damage, severe lupus pneumonitis, severe lupus hepatitis, or severe vasculitis, etc., and deemed unsuitable for participation by the investigator. 3. Presence of clinically significant central nervous system diseases or pathological changes not attributable to lupus prior to screening, including but not limited to: cerebrovascular accident, aneurysm, epilepsy, convulsions/seizures, aphasia, stroke, severe brain injury, dementia, Parkinson's disease, cerebellar disease, organic brain syndrome, or psychiatric illness. 4. History of allogeneic bone marrow or stem cell transplantation, or solid organ transplantation (e.g., kidney, lung, heart, liver), or planned such transplantation in the future. 5. For IIM patients: Presence of severe rhabdomyolysis or CK level >=120 × ULN at screening. 6. For MG patients: Presence of uncontrolled myasthenic crisis within 2 weeks prior to screening. 7. History of clinically significant cardiovascular dysfunction within 12 months prior to screening, including but not limited to: New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV heart failure, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, uncontrolled or symptomatic atrial arrhythmia, any ventricular arrhythmia. 8. Presence of significant pulmonary or cardiac manifestations at screening, such as pericarditis, pleural effusion, deemed unsuitable for participation by the investigator. 9. Patients with severe asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Patients with mild or moderate asthma or COPD receiving stable treatment may be enrolled. 10. History of malignancy within 5 years prior to signing the ICF, except for adequately treated or surgically resected non-melanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ (e.g., cervical, bladder, breast) with no evidence of residual disease. 11. Pregnant or lactating women. 12. History of recurrent infections requiring hospitalization and intravenous antibiotic therapy (e.g., three or more episodes of the same type of infection within the past year). 13. Active infection requiring systemic treatment within 2 weeks prior to lymphodepletion, such as infectious pneumonia, tuberculosis, etc. 14. Positive Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), or positive Hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb) with positive peripheral blood Hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA test; positive Hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody with positive peripheral blood HCV RNA; positive Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) antibody; positive syphilis antibody. 15. Administration of a live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks prior to treatment, or planned administration during the study. 16. Use of high-dose corticosteroids (prednisone >=60 mg/day or equivalent) within 4 weeks prior to treatment, or inability to taper prednisone to <=10 mg/day by 3 days prior to lymphodepletion. 17. Inability to taper or wash out background therapies as specified in Table 3 prior to treatment. 18. Currently receiving renal replacement therapy within 3 months prior to screening or expected to require renal replacement therapy during the study period. 19. History of drug or alcohol abuse within 1 year prior to screening. 20. History or evidence of suicidal ideation within 6 months prior to screening, or any suicidal behavior within 12 months prior to screening, considered by the investigator to present a significant suicide risk. 21. Use of another investigational drug within 4 weeks prior to screening or within 5 half-lives (whichever is longer). 22. History of hypersensitivity or life-threatening reaction to any component or formulation of the investigational product. Refer to the Investigator's Brochure (IB) for details on components. 23. Any condition that, in the investigator's judgment, could affect study participation, pose a safety risk to the patient, or potentially confound the interpretation of study results.
